word_order: SOV — verbs consistently appear clause-final, e.g. 'ごんは...ぬかるみみちを歩いていきました' (subject-object-verb).
punctuation_present: always — 。、「」are used throughout to mark sentence and quotation boundaries
register: read-aloud narrative prose (children's literary story, third-person narration with embedded dialogue)
clause_boundary_signals: 、 (comma, often marking clause break after -te form or topic phrase)
verb + た。 / だ。 / ます。 (finite past/polite sentence endings)
-て form followed by comma or new clause (e.g. 歩いていきました、のぞいてみました)
ので / から (causal clause boundary)
と (quotation-closing particle before verbs like 言いました, 思いました)
non_boundary_traps: の (genitive/nominalizer, not a topic or clause marker, e.g. '山の霊', '国中で一番高い山')
て-form mid-sentence (連用形) which chains clauses without ending them, e.g. '歩いていきました' is one clause not two
が used as subject marker vs. conjunction 'but' — same character different function
、 inside quoted speech that does not end the sentence
だ / です before another clause continuation (e.g. '～だとみえて')
target_language_risks: Japanese frequently omits subjects/pronouns; Korean also allows omission but referent tracking must be preserved across segments or ambiguity arises
Honorific and speech-level nuances (敬語) in dialogue must be mapped to appropriate Korean speech levels (해요체/합니다체) consistently
Nested quotations with 「」 can be split incorrectly, breaking the reported-speech frame if segmented mid-quote
-te form chains (e.g. 歩いていきました) may be split prematurely, losing the single continuous action reading in Korean's equally chained -고/-며 structure
Sentence-final auxiliary verbs (ました, でした) carry tense/aspect that must stay attached to the main verb; premature segmentation can strand tense information
notes_for_prompt_writer: Treat 。and closing 」as the strongest boundary signals; treat 、 as a weak, context-dependent boundary that often follows -te forms or topic markers and should not trigger a split unless a full clause (with its own verb) precedes it. Keep quoted speech blocks intact when possible, since translating a fragment of dialogue without its closing quote or attribution verb (言いました, 思いました) breaks meaning in Korean. Because Japanese is head-final and consistently SOV like Korean, structural reordering is minimal, but subject/topic ellipsis requires carrying context forward across segments.
